area: analytics (Session, History, Projects, Equipment Stats, Science, Diagnostics) + science screen

findings.title: Session tab reports Duration "0s" for any session that has no end_time
findings.what_happened: Reviewing seeded session 3 (Night C - M31, status in_progress, start 2026-07-30 20:30Z, end_time NULL, 3 light frames spanning 20.3 minutes), the summary strip shows DURATION 0s while the charts beside it plot a 20-minute time axis.
findings.expected: A session with no end time should say "in progress" / "--", or compute now-minus-start. 0s is a false statement contradicted by the charts on the same card.
findings.repro: sqlite3 seed an imaging_sessions row with end_time NULL and captured_images spanning 20 min; restart app; Analytics > Session; the review bar auto-selects that session.
findings.proposed_fix: When endTime is null, use DateTime.now() for a session whose status is in_progress, else render Unfinished.

findings.title: Guiding chart Y axis draws two labels on top of each other when the series is flat
findings.what_happened: With all three frames at guiding RMS 0.70, the Guiding performance axis renders 0.25 and 0.20 overlapping into an illegible blob at the bottom of the axis.
findings.expected: Axis labels never overlap - which is exactly what NiceAxis was written to guarantee.
findings.repro: Seed frames with identical guiding_rms_total (0.70); Analytics > Session; look at the bottom-left of the Guiding performance chart.
findings.proposed_fix: The zero-variance branch returns min = centre - 2*interval without snapping to a tick multiple (0.70 - 0.50 = 0.20 with interval 0.25), so the boundary label lands 0.05 from the 0.25 tick. Snap: min = (centre/interval).floor()*interval - 2*interval, same for max - the same snapping the varying branch already does.

findings.title: The four Session charts are computed over three different frame populations; the guiding chart includes frames the app rejected
findings.what_happened: For seeded session 1 (12 light frames, 10 accepted + 2 rejected with rms 4.2", plus 4 darks) the four charts on one card report n=10 (Image quality), n=12 (Guiding performance), n=12 (Focus drift) and n=16 (Sensor temperature). The guiding headline therefore reads median 0.8 / p90 3.9 / range 0.5-4.2 and the 1" warning line is breached, when every accepted frame guided between 0.50" and 0.95". The temperature chart silently mixes in the 4 dark frames.
findings.expected: All four charts on the session card should plot the same, stated population. HfrChart filters isAccepted; the other three do not, and none filters frameType==light. A p90 of 3.9" for a session whose accepted-frame p90 is 0.905" is a wrong number a user would act on (they would go hunting for a guiding fault that does not exist).
findings.repro: Seed session 1 with 10 accepted lights (rms .50-.95), 2 rejected lights (rms 4.2, hfr 9.9, focuser 15100) and 4 darks (sensor_temp only). Restart. Analytics > Session > Reviewing > Night A - M31. Compare the n= counts in the four chart headers.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-analytics-08-s1.png - EXPOSURES 10/12 in the strip; chart headers n 10 / 12 / 12 / 16
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/session_chart.dart:375 (HfrChart filters isAccepted), :400 TemperatureChart, :425 GuidingRmsChart, :453 FocuserPositionChart (no filter at all)
findings.proposed_fix: Filter one population in _SessionTab.chartGrid (accepted lights) and pass it to all four charts, or give every chart the same `.where((i)=>i.isAccepted && i.frameType==light)` predicate. If rejected frames are wanted, draw them as a distinct marker series and say so in the header.

findings.title: Captured Images grades dark/calibration frames as "Good", inflating the session quality summary
findings.what_happened: Session 1 contains 12 lights (8 good, 2 needs-review, 2 poor) and 4 darks with no HFR/star-count/guiding metrics. The summary chips read Good: 12 / Needs Review: 2 / Poor: 2 / Total: 16. Scrolling the rail to the end shows the 4 darks rendered with a green GOOD badge and "75 score", indistinguishable from light frames except for a "—" filter.
findings.expected: The Captured Images summary on the Session tab should count light frames only, or at minimum not assert a quality grade for a frame that has no quality measurement. "Good: 12" is a false count - only 8 frames were assessed good.
findings.repro: Seed session 1 with 12 lights + 4 darks (darks: sensor_temp only, hfr/star_count/guiding NULL). Restart. Analytics > Session > Night A - M31, scroll to Captured Images; shift+wheel the rail to its right end.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-analytics-11.png (chips Good: 12 / Total: 16) and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-analytics-15.png (the 4 trailing darks badged GOOD / 75 score)
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/frame_quality_assessment_service.dart:112 `var advisoryScore = image.qualityScore ?? 75.0;` - a frame with every metric null scores 75 and falls through to FrameQualityLevel.good; packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/image_thumbnail_strip.dart:90 assesses widget.images unfiltered
findings.proposed_fix: assessBatch should return a distinct `unassessed` level when hfr, starCount, guidingRms and qualityScore are all null, and the strip should either exclude non-light frames or badge them by frame type.

findings.title: The Captured Images thumbnail rail cannot be scrolled with an ordinary mouse wheel and has no scrollbar
findings.what_happened: With 16 frames in the session only 12 thumbnails fit. Pointing at the rail and turning the wheel scrolls the PAGE, not the rail; the remaining 4 frames stay off-screen. Only a horizontal-wheel / shift+wheel gesture moved it. There is no scrollbar and no left/right affordance.
findings.expected: On desktop, a horizontal rail must be reachable with the wheel a user actually has - either map vertical wheel to the rail, or show a Scrollbar and arrow affordances. A 200-frame night is unusable otherwise.
findings.repro: Analytics > Session > Night A - M31; hover the Captured Images rail; wheel down (page scrolls). Shift+wheel to reveal the trailing frames.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/image_thumbnail_strip.dart:178 ListView.builder(scrollDirection: Axis.horizontal) with no Scrollbar and default desktop ScrollBehavior
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap in a Scrollbar(thumbVisibility: true) and add a Listener that maps PointerScrollEvent.dy onto the horizontal controller, as the app already does for the sequencer node rail.

findings.title: Exported FWHM is fabricated from HFR with the wrong factor (2.35x instead of 2x), overstating FWHM by 18%
findings.what_happened: History > Night A - M31 > Export CSV wrote /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/Night A - M31_2026-08-01T14-40-26.csv with a populated "FWHM (px)" column - 4.70, 5.17, 5.64 - even though captured_images.fwhm is NULL for every one of those rows. The values are HFR * 2.35.
findings.expected: For a Gaussian PSF the half-flux radius is 1.1774*sigma and FWHM = 2.3548*sigma, so FWHM = 2.00 * HFR. Multiplying HFR by 2.3548 treats HFR as sigma and inflates every reported FWHM by 17.7% (HFR 2.00 px -> 4.70" reported vs 4.00" true). Worse, the real `fwhm` column measured by the pipeline is ignored and overwritten by the derived number, and nothing in the CSV says the value is derived.
findings.repro: Analytics > History > click Night A - M31 > click the spreadsheet icon; open the CSV. HFR column x 2.35 == FWHM column exactly.
findings.evidence: /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/Night A - M31_2026-08-01T14-40-26.csv rows s1_000..s1_009; DB: select hfr,fwhm from captured_images where session_id=1 -> fwhm all NULL
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/session_export_service.dart:69-70 and :171; same factor in session_report_service.dart:301 (meanFwhm), capture_preview_loader.dart:180 (live capture FWHM readout), session_report.dart:36
findings.proposed_fix: Use image.fwhm when present; otherwise derive FWHM = 2.0 * HFR and label the column "FWHM (px, derived from HFR)". Fix the constant in all four call sites - the live capture readout is showing the same inflated number during a run.

findings.title: History and Session disagree about the same session: 46h 2m elapsed vs 0s duration
findings.what_happened: Session 3 (no end_time, 3 frames over 20 minutes) reads "46h 2m elapsed" on the History card and "DURATION 0s" on the Session tab, at the same moment, in the same app.
findings.expected: One answer, and neither of these. History uses DateTime.now()-startTime for any session without an end time, so a session the app failed to close (crash, power loss - the exact case this matters) accrues fictional elapsed time forever; the Session tab uses 0.
findings.repro: Seed an imaging_sessions row with end_time NULL. Analytics > History (46h 2m) then Analytics > Session with that session selected (0s).
findings.proposed_fix: Share one helper: elapsed = (endTime ?? lastFrameCapturedAt ?? startTime) - startTime, and render an explicit unfinished badge when endTime is null rather than a number.

findings.title: Session detail dialog says "Total Exposures 12" and "Images (16)" in the same panel
findings.what_happened: For Night A - M31 the Statistics row reads Total Exposures 12 / Successful 10 / Failed 2, and the heading immediately below reads Images (16) with chips Good: 12 / Needs Review: 2 / Poor: 2 / Total: 16.
findings.expected: Two counts of the same thing on one card should agree or be labelled differently. The stats row comes from the denormalised imaging_sessions counters (light frames), the image list from captured_images (lights + calibration frames). Nothing tells the user which is which.
findings.proposed_fix: Label the list "Frames (16, incl. 4 calibration)" or scope both to light frames.

findings.title: Captured Images thumbnails are inert - tapping a frame does nothing anywhere in Analytics
findings.what_happened: Clicking a thumbnail in the Session tab and in the session detail dialog produces no reaction: no preview, no grade action, no metadata. ImageThumbnailStrip takes an onImageTap callback and no caller in the app passes one.
findings.expected: A gallery of the night frames is the obvious place to enlarge a frame, read its FITS header, or accept/reject it. NINA and the ASIAIR both open the frame from the thumbnail. The ImageGraderDialog that would do this exists but is reachable only from the Science tab.
findings.repro: Analytics > Session > Night A - M31; click any thumbnail. Nothing happens. Same in History > session detail.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-analytics-16-grader.png (screen unchanged after the click); grep shows no call site passes onImageTap
findings.proposed_fix: Pass onImageTap that opens ImageGraderDialog (or a frame inspector) from both call sites.

findings.title: Equipment Stats: half of the tab is permanently "Not tracked"
findings.what_happened: With a full session history seeded, Mount shows Total Slews / Total Tracking Time / Meridian Flips = Not tracked, Focuser shows Total Movements = Not tracked, Guider shows Total Guide Time and Star Lost Events = Not tracked. Six of the twelve figures are hardcoded strings.
findings.expected: An "Equipment Stats" tab whose Mount card contains no numbers at all is not worth a tab. Several of these are already derivable from data the app stores: meridian flips are recorded as sequencer decisions/narrator events, guide time and star-lost from guide_rms_history, focuser movements from focus_models/autofocus runs.
findings.repro: Analytics > Equipment Stats with 3 sessions and 27 frames seeded.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-analytics-empty-EquipStats.png (empty profile) and the same six labels with data present
findings.proposed_fix: Either wire the six to the tables that already hold the data, or drop the Mount card and rename the tab to what it measures (camera + focus + guiding quality).

findings.title: Projects header "Active This Month" counts targets, not sessions, and resets on the 1st
findings.what_happened: With three imaging sessions on Jul 25/28/30 and today Aug 1, the Projects header reads "0 Active This Month". Even inside the month it can never exceed the number of targets: the code counts PROJECTS whose lastSessionAt is after the 1st (the variable is even named sessionsThisMonth), so twenty nights on one target still shows 1.
findings.expected: Either a session count over a rolling 30 nights (astronomers do not care about calendar-month boundaries; an observing run straddles them), or a label that says what it counts ("Targets active this month").
findings.repro: Analytics > Projects with sessions dated Jul 25/28/30 and system date Aug 1.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-analytics-26-projects.png and -30-projects3.png (0 Active This Month beside 1.5h Total Integration)
findings.proposed_fix: Count sessions in the last 30 days: sessions.where((s)=>s.startTime.isAfter(now.subtract(Duration(days:30)))).length, and relabel "Nights (30d)".

findings.title: Campaign Rollup shows "Effective imaging 0.0%" when no session in the campaign has closed
findings.what_happened: meanEffectiveImagingFraction is `simpleMean(efficiencyInputs) ?? 0.0` and efficiencyInputs only accepts sessions with an end_time. A campaign whose only session is still open therefore renders "Effective imaging 0.0%" - a measured-looking claim that no imaging happened - while the neighbouring "Mean seeing" correctly renders "-" for the same missing-data case.
findings.expected: "-", as the tile beside it already does for absent data.
findings.repro: Observed in the running app for M31 (12.8%, correctly excluding the open session Night C). The all-open case is the same code path with an empty efficiencyInputs list; not reproduced live because every seeded target also had a closed session.
findings.evidence: source-only for the 0.0% case; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-analytics-31-campaign.png confirms the exclusion rule live (12.8% == session 1 alone, not 20.5% over both sessions)
findings.proposed_fix: Make meanEffectiveImagingFraction nullable and render - like Mean seeing.

findings.title: Insights invents a guiding baseline of 0.1 arcsec when there is no history, so every user with <=5 sessions is told their guiding degraded 7x
findings.what_happened: The Science tab Insights panel showed 'Guiding degradation - Recent guiding RMS is 7.20x the historical baseline. Check balance, flexure, and backlash.' and 'Focus quality drift - Recent median HFR is elevated versus the longer-term baseline.' The five seeded sessions have avgGuidingRms 0.60/0.55/0.70/1.10/0.65 (mean 0.72) and there is NO older session at all - guiding never degraded, and the newest session (0.55) is the best of the five.
findings.expected: With no baseline sessions, no baseline claim. The panel should stay silent (or say 'not enough history') instead of asserting a 7.2x regression and deducting 32 points from the equipment health score.
findings.repro: Seed exactly 5 imaging_sessions with avg_guiding_rms 0.65/1.10/0.70/0.55/0.60 and avg_hfr 2.90/4.20/3.00/2.50/2.20. Restart. Analytics > Science > scroll to Insights.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-analytics-41.png. Arithmetic proof: baseline = recentSessions.skip(5).take(10) is EMPTY with 5 sessions, _mean([]) = 0.0, .clamp(0.1,100.0) = 0.1; mean recent guiding 3.60/5 = 0.72; 0.72/0.1 = 7.20 - exactly the number on screen.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/equipment_health_service.dart:200 (baseline = skip(5).take(10)), :205-213 (.clamp(0.1,100.0) turns 'no data' into 0.1), :222 and :234 (the two triggers), _mean at :324
findings.proposed_fix: Make the baselines nullable: if the baseline window is empty, skip both insights entirely and do not deduct score. The clamp exists to avoid divide-by-zero; the real fix is to not divide when there is nothing to divide by.

findings.title: Sequencer crash-recovery checkpoint is stored outside the profile data dir, so one instance offers to resume another instance's sequence
findings.what_happened: On startup this audit instance (SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR/SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR = /tmp/ns-audit/r-analytics/data, with ZERO rows in sequences and sequence_checkpoints) showed 'Recover Sequence? A previous sequence was interrupted and can be resumed - Sequence: New Sequence, Saved 0m ago, Completed 4 frames (0m integration)'. The checkpoint it read is /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint, written by a DIFFERENT concurrently-running instance.
findings.expected: Crash recovery must be scoped to the instance/profile that wrote it. Offering to resume a sequence whose id does not exist in this database is a data-integrity hazard: on a machine that runs both the desktop app and the headless host (a shipped configuration) the two silently clobber each other's recovery state, and Resume would restart the wrong run. Note also the self-contradictory summary line 'Completed 4 frames (0m integration)'.
findings.repro: Run two Skotiq desktop instances with different SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR values. Build a sequence in one. Restart the other: it offers to recover the first one's sequence.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-analytics-33-sci2.png; sqlite3 <profile db> 'select * from sequence_checkpoints' -> 0 rows, 'select * from sequences' -> 0 rows; the checkpoint file in ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop was last written at 14:50 by another pid
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:347 getApplicationSupportDirectory() is passed to sequencerSetCheckpointDir, ignoring SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR; native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/checkpoint.rs:516
findings.proposed_fix: Derive the checkpoint dir from the same root as the database (SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR when set), and stamp the checkpoint with the database path/instance id so a mismatched checkpoint is ignored rather than offered.

findings.title: 'Recover Sequence?' modal has no way out except Discard (destructive) or Resume (acts)
findings.what_happened: The recovery dialog offers only Discard and Resume; Escape does not dismiss it and there is no barrier dismiss. The Incomplete Sessions dialog on the same startup path does offer 'Decide Later'.
findings.expected: A user who wants to look at the sequence before deciding is forced to destroy the checkpoint or start a run. Match the sibling dialog and offer 'Decide later'.
findings.repro: Launch with a checkpoint present; press Escape - dialog remains.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a third action that leaves the checkpoint on disk and closes the dialog, as the Incomplete Sessions dialog does.

findings.title: Recovering a stale session stamps end_time = now, inflating its duration by days
findings.what_happened: Session 3 (Night C - M31, last frame 2026-07-30 20:55Z) was left status='active'. After the startup recovery flow ran it became status='aborted' with end_time = 2026-08-01 18:52Z - the moment of recovery, 46 hours after the last frame. Its History card and every derived statistic (wall clock, effective imaging, campaign efficiency) now use a 46-hour session.
findings.expected: Closing an abandoned session should set end_time to the last captured frame's timestamp, not to the clock at recovery time. Otherwise one crash permanently corrupts the night's duration and drags the target's campaign efficiency toward zero.
findings.repro: Seed a session with status='active', end_time NULL and frames ending 2 days ago. Restart the app, work through the Incomplete Sessions dialog. sqlite3: select status,end_time from imaging_sessions where id=3 -> aborted, <now>.
findings.evidence: DB before: 3|Night C - M31|active|(null); after: 3|Night C - M31|aborted|1785610346 (2026-08-01 18:52:26Z) while the session's last frame is at 1785440100 (2026-07-30 20:55Z)
findings.where: session recovery path in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/session_service.dart (stale 'active' session handling around :431)
findings.proposed_fix: end_time = max(last captured_images.captured_at for the session, start_time) when force-closing a recovered session.

findings.title: Science tab says 'Science idle - Waiting for the first captured frame' while the session under analysis has 120 frames
findings.what_happened: With Night D - V-Test (120 frames, 100% solved, full photometry) selected in the Analysing bar, the banner directly beneath reads 'Science idle / Waiting for the first captured frame', immediately above 'Plate solve health 100% - 120 of 120 solved'.
findings.expected: The banner reports the in-memory pipeline state for the current app process, which is empty after a restart. When the tab is reviewing a historical session it should say so ('Reviewing stored results') rather than claim no frame has been captured.
findings.repro: Restart the app, Analytics > Science, select a past session with frames.
findings.proposed_fix: When the selected session is not the live one, render a review-mode subtitle keyed off the stored product counts instead of the live pipeline history.

findings.title: Science tab defaults to the newest session even when it has no science data
findings.what_happened: After adding a 2-frame session (Night E - M13, no photometry, no solves) that started later than the 120-frame photometry night, the Science tab opened on Night E and showed '0% - 0 of 2 solved', 'Warming up', and the empty-state 'Turn pretty pictures into real measurements'. The 120-frame calibrated night was two clicks away in a dropdown.
findings.expected: The default should be the most recent session that actually has science products. Otherwise a user who took two test frames after a long photometry run comes back to an empty Science tab.
findings.repro: Analytics > Science with sessions 4 (120 frames, solved+photometry) and 5 (2 frames, nothing) where 5 starts later.
findings.proposed_fix: Default to the newest session with >0 photometry measurements or >0 solved frames; fall back to newest overall.
